intro: Biggest rank disagreements between the SEI board and SP+, 2026 season: from the SP+ top 15 and from our own top 15.

teams.explanation: The widest gap on the board this week, and the cleanest example of process beating the scoreboard: SEI #8, SP+ #53. The Seminoles sit 43rd in margin (+31) because a 27-24 loss to SMU and a 50-36 loss at Alabama keep the points ugly — but the play-by-play is top-10 quality: PPA +1.57 SD, red-zone arrival +1.62, TD rate +1.64. SP+'s margin engine punishes the Alabama blowout; we price the drives that produced it.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #43 (margin +31) but SEI #8.
SP+ halves: off #35, def #74.
Strongest metrics: TD% +1.64, RZ arr +1.62, PPA +1.57.

teams.explanation: SP+ has the Wildcats #50, with a #59 offense; our offense half is #5 — PPA +2.10, success rate +1.83, red-zone TD rate +1.89. The 34-13 win over Penn State and 41-7 over Colorado were per-play dominant; the 23-29 loss at Indiana was six points. Small sample caveat: three FBS games, already shrunk toward the mean. If the profile holds, SP+ is chasing, not leading.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #30 (margin +49) but SEI #7.
Defense drives the gap: SEI off #5 vs def #26.
SP+ halves: off #59, def #34.
Strongest metrics: PPA +2.10, RZ TD% +1.89, SR +1.83.

teams.explanation: SP+ #51 with an #84 offense; we have the Badgers #12 on PPA +1.74, success rate +1.62 and explosiveness +1.62. The scoreboard story is a 41-13 loss at Notre Dame and a two-point win at Penn State — margin-of-victory hates both. Strip the excluded Eastern Michigan blowout and the remaining margins are thin, but the per-play rates against real defenses are genuinely good.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #31 (margin +48) but SEI #12.
SP+ halves: off #84, def #19.
Strongest metrics: PPA +1.74, SR +1.62, Exp +1.62.

teams.explanation: SP+ #15, us #45 — the widest gap on the board. The Cornhuskers sit 6th in scoring margin (+120), but our defense half ranks 97th: opponents post roughly average success rate and PPA against them, it just hasn't shown up on the scoreboard against Ohio, Bowling Green, Michigan State and Maryland. SP+'s #22 defensive grade is a margin-of-victory artifact — the plays have been there even if the points haven't. If the efficiency profile is the true one, Nebraska's margin catches down, not up.
hints: Scoreboard outran process: margin rank #6 (margin +120) but SEI #45.
Defense drives the gap: SEI off #15 vs def #97.
SP+ halves: off #20, def #22.
Strongest metrics: TD% +1.97, RZ TD% +1.94, PPA +1.53.
Weakest metrics: FG% -2.25.

teams.explanation: SP+ has the Bulldogs #1 overall and #1 on both halves; we have them #25 with a #60 defense. The scoreboard outruns the process: 4th in margin (+130), but no defensive metric stands out as elite in our halves — Georgia is winning on offensive efficiency (#10, best in the field in success rate and takeaways away) plus finished drives, not by overwhelming opponents play by play at both ends. Blowout margins against Western Kentucky and Vanderbilt move SP+; they move us much less.
hints: Scoreboard outran process: margin rank #4 (margin +130) but SEI #25.
Defense drives the gap: SEI off #10 vs def #60.
SP+ halves: off #1, def #1.
Strongest metrics: SR +1.68, TO +1.62.

teams.explanation: SP+ ranks the Canes #5 (offense #8, defense #8); we have them #27 with defense #46. The 5-0 record and +129 margin — including a 41-13 win at Clemson — is exactly what margin-of-victory models reward. But the play-by-play profile is good, not elite: offense #17, defense #46, and stuff rate is a bottom-tier weakness (-1.50 SD). We think Clemson was a great game, not a representative one.
hints: Scoreboard outran process: margin rank #5 (margin +129) but SEI #27.
Defense drives the gap: SEI off #17 vs def #46.
SP+ halves: off #8, def #8.
Strongest metrics: TD% +1.54.
Weakest metrics: Stuff -1.50.

teams.explanation: SP+ sees a #14 team with a #14 offense; our offense half is #78. The engine metrics are the problem — explosiveness is a bottom-5% weakness (-1.93 SD) — while red-zone finishing is elite (+2.38 SD in RZ TD%): the Vols march slowly, then convert ruthlessly once they arrive, and the 20-17 loss to Texas shows how thin that margin is. SP+ prices the points scored; we price the play that produced them.
hints: Scoreboard outran process: margin rank #23 (margin +61) but SEI #36.
Offense drives the gap: SEI off #78 vs def #15.
SP+ halves: off #14, def #26.
Strongest metrics: RZ TD% +2.38, TD% +1.62.
Weakest metrics: Exp -1.93, FG% -1.75.

teams.explanation: The standing example from our own philosophy: SEI #9, SP+ #27. The Sooners' defense is our #3 — havoc +2.68 SD is the best single metric on this page — while the offense is #55 and the FBS-only margin is genuinely bad (losses to Michigan and Georgia). SP+ blends the halves into one rating and lands #27; our additive composite lets an elite defense carry a mediocre offense to #9. That is a design choice, and this is where it shows.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #48 (margin +24) but SEI #9.
Offense drives the gap: SEI off #55 vs def #3.
SP+ halves: off #75, def #5.
Strongest metrics: Havoc +2.68, TD% +2.18, PPA +2.13.
Weakest metrics: AR -1.80.

teams.explanation: The one case where the scoreboard undersells the profile: SEI #20 vs SP+ #8 despite a margin of only +13 (56th). The loss at Oklahoma State and the 34-27 win over Boise State keep the scoreboard ugly, but the process is solid — defense #25, and the 41-27 win at USC was a genuinely strong game on the road. SP+'s #8 leans on projection and prior; our #20 says the actual play is good but not elite, and offense #36 is the half to watch.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #56 (margin +13) but SEI #20.
SP+ halves: off #5, def #25.

teams.explanation: The two boards mostly agree here — SP+ #18, us #10 — and the small gap is close-game arithmetic: wins over South Carolina by 7 and Missouri by 7 give margin-of-victory models almost nothing, and the 56-23 Alabama loss drags the rest. Our offense half (#7, TD rate +2.07) carries them; SP+'s #47 defense is the number we trust less. Watch this one: the profile says the resume is better than the record.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #26 (margin +55) but SEI #10.
Defense drives the gap: SEI off #7 vs def #38.
SP+ halves: off #10, def #47.
